title: skillwright spec v2: one vault layout
summary: The v2 structure spec , the changes from v1 and the implementation plan, from PR #145, one block per rule or paragraph, for inline review.

blocks.text:
v2 has one goal: stable marketplace publishing, with transclusion and good
bundling. Its commands are `init`, `build`, `check` and `bump`.

This spec defines how skillwright reads a vault. A vault has one fixed layout.
The spec covers the folders, the root file, the notes, links, the frontmatter
rules and the output. The frontmatter keys themselves are in the
[[docs/reference/fields|field reference]], which is part of this spec.

The decisions behind this spec are in section 12. Edge cases are in
Appendix A. What v2
changes for a vault built with today's tool is in
[[docs/spec/v2-changes|v2-changes.md]].

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| reads | skillwright loads a file as source. |
| interprets | skillwright acts on a link, call, embed or plugin-root path in some text. Text that is not interpreted ships exactly as written. |
| component | A skill, agent or command (section 3). |
| container | A marketplace or a plugin. |
| pack | The folder a harness installs for one plugin (section 9). |
| an error | The build or check stops and exits non-zero. Nothing is written. |
| an error for a harness | The same: the whole build fails, even though only that harness's output has the problem. The message names the harness. |
| a warning | Printed. The build goes on and exits 0. |

- Stable: the layout (sections 1 to 3), the link and embed rules (sections 4
  and 5), the frontmatter fields (section 6) and what a pack holds (section 9).
  A breaking change to any of them makes a new version of this spec.

- There is no experimental layer. Flexibility is added later, as a new
  version.

1. The vault is the folder that holds both `skillwright.md` and a
   `marketplaces/` folder. That folder is the root. A vault looks like this:

blocks.code:
/ ├── skillwright.md the root file: shared settings ├── dist/ build output └── marketplaces/ └── / ├── .md the marketplace └── plugins/ └──

/ ├──

.md the plugin └── skills//.md

blocks.text:
2. `--vault <path>` names the root. Without it, skillwright finds the root in
   these steps:
   1. Start at the working directory.
   2. If the folder holds both `skillwright.md` and `marketplaces/`, it is the
      root. Stop.
   3. Otherwise move to the parent folder and repeat step 2.
   4. At the top of the file system, fail. The error names any
      `skillwright.md` passed over on the way.

   Any other `skillwright.md`, such as a skill's note, is passed over (see
   Appendix A1).

3. v2 does not support a vault inside a larger notes vault. At the root, only
   `skillwright.md` and `marketplaces/` are read, and `dist/` is written
   (section 9). Only the root's direct children are checked. A `skills/`,
   `agents/`, `commands/`, `hooks/` or `plugins/` folder there is refused
   (section 11 case 4). Anything else at the root is left alone and not read,
   at any depth, such as `notes/` or `notes/marketplaces/`.
A complete root file, with every key it may hold:

blocks.code:
---
# Shared defaults. Every marketplace and plugin inherits these unless it
# sets its own.
author: Ada Lovelace            # or {name, email, url}
license: MIT                    # an SPDX expression
repository: https://github.com/acme/skills
homepage: https://acme.dev/skills
targets: [claude, codex]        # which harnesses get each component; absent means all
claude: {}                      # harness blocks: fields only that harness reads (section 8)
codex: {}
cursor: {}                      # {naming: bare} keeps plain skill names (section 8)
pi: {}                          # {naming: bare} likewise

# Tool settings.
build:
  harnesses: [claude, codex, cursor, pi]   # which harnesses to build; absent means all
  bump:
    patch: increment                       # or timestamp (section 10 rule 4)
---

blocks.text:
1. `skillwright.md` exists only at the root. Its body is not read. It is the
   only configuration file.

2. It holds two kinds of key:
   - the shared defaults, which are the keys the key table marks as
     inherited (section 7 rule 1);
   - `build:`, the tool settings.

3. A key the key table does not list warns and is ignored, as
   [[docs/decisions/D-KVMB-bare-keys-by-default|D-KVMB]] says. There is one
   exception: `workspace` is a removed key and is refused (section 11).

4. A key the table lists but does not mark as inherited is refused here. The error names the note kinds that accept it: | Key | Belongs in | |---|---| | `owner` | a marketplace note, `.md` | | `keywords`, `category` | a plugin note, `

.md` | | `description`, `version`, `display_name` | a marketplace or plugin note |

5. These `build:` keys are refused (section 11): `out`, `patterns`,
   `exclude`, `assets`, `hooks`, `destinations`, `scan_locations`,
   `launcher_path` and `namespace`. Any other unknown `build:` key warns.

blocks.code:
/ ├── skillwright.md tool settings (build:) and shared defaults ├── dist/ output, written by build (section 9) └── marketplaces/ └── / ├── .md the marketplace's note └── plugins/ └──

/ ├──

.md the plugin's note ├── CHANGELOG.md optional, copied into each pack ├── references/ shared docs, ship as references/ ├── scripts/ shared code, ship as scripts/ ├── assets/ shared output files, ship as assets/ ├── skills// │ ├── .md │ ├── references/ │ ├── scripts/ │ └── assets/ ├── agents//.md ├── commands//.md └── hooks/ └── hooks.json optional: the plugin's hooks (decision D4)

blocks.text:
The layout follows the recommended practice of the Agent Skills standard. A
skill is a folder with its entry note and optional `references/`, `scripts/`
and `assets/` folders. Relative paths resolve from the skill's folder
(harness-reference: `Agent Skills Agent Skills format`,
`Agent Skills Relative paths in SKILL.md`).

1. Every note is `<name>.md` in a folder of the same name. There is no other
   entry form. A flat `<name>.md` directly in a kind folder (`skills/`,
   `agents/`, `commands/`) is refused, and so is `SKILL.md`.

2. Position alone decides what a note is: | Folder | It is | |---|---| | `marketplaces//` | a marketplace | | `marketplaces//plugins/

/` | a plugin | | `

/skills//`, `

/agents//`, `

/commands//` | a component of that kind | | `

/hooks/` | the plugin's hooks folder: `hooks.json` only, no components | Frontmatter never decides kind, plugin or marketplace.

3. Each marketplace folder must hold `.md`, and each plugin folder `

.md`. A missing note is an error that names the path it expects. The body of a container note is not interpreted and does not ship. It is for the author.

4. The folder's name is the note's name. The build writes it as the `name`
   each harness reads, such as the `name` in `SKILL.md`. There is no `name`
   key: a note that sets one is refused, and the error says to delete it.

6. Six names are reserved and refused for any marketplace, plugin or
   component: `marketplaces`, `plugins`, `skills`, `agents`, `commands` and
   `hooks`. A folder with one of these names is taken as a structure folder,
   so in a name position it is out of place (section 11).

7. Names are unique within a plugin, across all kinds. A skill and a command
   with one name in one plugin are refused, naming both. The same name in two
   plugins, or two marketplaces, is allowed.

8. Every note at a component position is a component. A skill, command or
   agent needs a `description`, because harnesses use it to pick the
   component. A missing `description` is an error that `build` and `check`
   report.

9. A component exists only inside a plugin, and a plugin only inside a
   marketplace. A `skills/`, `plugins/` or other kind folder anywhere else is
   an error (section 11).

10. One skill may be copied into two marketplaces. Each copy is its own
    component. There is no shared folder across plugins.
11. `check` warns when a plugin's `version` has no entry in its `CHANGELOG.md`.

Below the root, each folder holds a fixed set of entries. Anything else is an
error that names the file and lists what the folder may hold.
Some entries are skipped everywhere, and one is an error:

| Entry | Result |
|---|---|
| A name that starts with `.`, such as `.DS_Store`, `.git` or `.obsidian` | Skipped: never read, never shipped, never an error |
| `node_modules/` | Skipped |
| `.mcp.json` in a plugin folder | An error: v2 has no home for it (decision D7) |

| Folder | May hold | |---|---| | The root | `skillwright.md`, `marketplaces/`, `dist/`. Anything else is left alone and not read, except the refused names of section 11 case 4. | | `marketplaces/` | Marketplace folders only. | | `marketplaces//` | `.md`, `plugins/`. | | `plugins/` | Plugin folders only. | | `plugins/

/` | `

.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `hooks/`, and the never-ship folders `src/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, `fixtures/` (rule 15). | | `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` | Component folders only. | | `hooks/` | `hooks.json` only. A folder or any other file in it is an error. | | `skills//` | `.md`, `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`, and the never-ship folders `src/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, `fixtures/`. | | `agents//`, `commands//` | Their note, and the never-ship folders `docs/`, `tests/`, `fixtures/`. |
So a `README.md` in `marketplaces/` or in `skills/` is an error.

12. In a skill, each folder has one job, and each ships inside the skill's
    folder under the same name:

    | Folder | Holds |
    |---|---|
    | `references/` | Docs the agent reads into context when it needs them. |
    | `scripts/` | Code the agent runs. |
    | `assets/` | Files used in output, such as templates, images and fonts. |

13. An agent or command installs as a single file, so it has no folder of
    its own to ship. It uses the plugin's shared folders.

14. A plugin's `references/`, `scripts/` and `assets/` are shared by every
    component in the plugin. Each ships under the same name at the pack root.
    Nothing is flattened: `assets/x` ships as `assets/x`.

blocks.code:
plugins/tools/
├── scripts/deploy.sh        shared: ships as <pack>/scripts/deploy.sh
├── commands/deploy/
│   └── deploy.md            one file: <pack>/commands/deploy.md
└── skills/review/
    ├── review.md            ships as <pack>/skills/review/SKILL.md
    └── scripts/lint.sh      the skill's own: ships inside its folder

blocks.text:
15. The never-ship folders never ship, and nothing may link or embed into
    them:

    | Folder | May sit in |
    |---|---|
    | `docs/`, `tests/`, `fixtures/` | a plugin or component folder |
    | `src/` | a plugin or skill folder |

    The names count only directly in a plugin or component folder. Inside
    `references/`, `scripts/` or `assets/` they are ordinary folders and ship
    (Appendix A8).

16. skillwright does not run builds. It only copies what is already in
    `scripts/`, `references/` and `assets/`. A built file is made in these
    steps:
    1. Its source sits in `src/`, or outside the vault.
    2. The author's own build step, such as `bun build` or a moon task, writes
       the output into the plugin's or skill's `scripts/`, `references/` or
       `assets/`.
    3. `skillwright build` copies it into each pack.

blocks.code:
plugins/tools/
├── src/cli.ts           source: never ships
├── scripts/tool.js      written by `bun build src/cli.ts`, before skillwright build
└── skills/review/
    └── review.md        calls ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool.js

blocks.text:
`scripts/tool.js` ships as `<pack>/scripts/tool.js`. Section 4 rules 15 to
    26 write the skill's `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool.js` for each harness.

17. Files inside `references/`, `scripts/` and `assets/` may be laid out in any
    folders below them. `scripts/` keeps each file's exec bit.
The syntax decides what a token is, not its target:

| You write | It is | What the build does |
|---|---|---|
| `/[[x]]` | A call (rule 8) | Writes the harness's call string |
| `![[x]]` | An embed (section 5) | Inlines the note, section or file |
| `[[x]]`, `[text](relative/path.md)` | A link | Checks the target is in scope, rewrites the path |
| `[text](https://…)`, `<https://…>`, `mailto:` and any other URL with a scheme | An external link | Ships as written, not checked |
| `[text](#heading)` | A link within the same file | Ships as written, not checked |
| `[text](/abs/path)` or `[text](file:…)` | A path outside the vault | Refused |
| `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path>` | A plugin-root path (rules 15 to 26) | Checks the file ships, rewrites per harness, inside code too |
| Anything in a code span or fenced block | Literal (rule 12) | Ships as written, with two exceptions (rule 12) |

A plugin-root path is interpreted inside code, because a command in a code
block is where it is used. Source and output:

blocks.code: Run `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool.js --check`.

blocks.text:
| Pack | Ships as |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | ``Run `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool.js --check`.`` |
| Codex, Cursor, Pi | ``Run `../../scripts/tool.js --check`.`` |

On Codex, Cursor and Pi the model resolves the relative path before it runs
the command (rule 19).

An external link is never fetched or checked, so a dead URL is not an error.
An embed resolves by the same scope rules as a link. The rules apply to a
component's note and to every Markdown file it ships.

1. Each marketplace builds self-contained. A link, an embed or a shipped file
   that resolves outside `marketplaces/<m>/` is an error.

2. Every path is checked by its real path, with symlinks resolved. A symlink
   whose target lies outside the scope it is checked against is refused, in
   the same way as a link that spells that target.

blocks.title: Scope of a link from a component

blocks.text:
| Link target | Rule |
|---|---|
| A file in the component's own folder | Ships as written, relative. |
| A file in the plugin's `references/`, `scripts/` or `assets/` | Allowed. Rewritten to its installed path at the pack root. |
| Another component's note, or a file in its folder, same plugin | Allowed. Rewritten to its installed path. A link to a skill's or command's note also warns (rule 7). |
| A component the harness's pack does not contain, such as any agent | An error for that harness. |
| A file in another plugin | Refused. |
| Anything outside `marketplaces/<m>/` | Refused. |

A call, `/[[name]]`, is not a link and copies nothing. Its scope is the whole
marketplace (rule 8, decision D2).
3. A name-only link, `[[name]]`, resolves in up to two steps:

blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  A["[[name]]"] --> B{"Step 1: the linking file's component folder"}
  B -- "one match" --> R1["that file"]
  B -- "no match" --> C{"Step 2: the plugin's shared folders and components"}
  B -- "two or more" --> E1["error: names each match"]
  C -- "one match" --> R2["that file or component"]
  C -- "no match" --> E2["error: link to nothing"]
  C -- "two or more" --> E3["error: names each match"]

blocks.text:
- It never resolves outside the plugin.
   - What each step matches:

     | Step | Matches |
     |---|---|
     | 1 | a file at any depth in the linking file's component folder |
     | 2 | a file at any depth in the plugin's shared `references/`, `scripts/` and `assets/`, and another component by its name only |

   - A file inside another component's folder is never found by name. Link it
     with a path (rule 4), such as `[[../setup/references/notes.md]]`.
   - `[[guide]]` matches `guide.md`. A name with an extension,
     `[[run.sh]]`, matches that exact file name.
   - `[[setup]]` matches the component `setup` in step 2.
   - A file that belongs to no component, such as one in the plugin's shared
     `references/`, has no step 1. It starts at step 2.

   An example. `author.md` contains:

blocks.code:
Follow [[guide]] and [[style]]. Then run [[setup]].
See [[x]].

blocks.text: The plugin `tools` holds:

blocks.code:
marketplaces/acme/plugins/tools/
├── references/
│   ├── guide.md                 shared
│   └── style.md                 shared
└── skills/
    ├── author/
    │   ├── author.md            the note that links
    │   └── references/guide.md  author's own
    └── setup/setup.md           another skill

blocks.text:
Each link resolves like this:

   | Link | Step 1: `skills/author/` | Step 2: shared folders and components | Result |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `[[guide]]` | `references/guide.md` | not searched | `author`'s own `guide.md`. The shared one is not used. |
   | `[[style]]` | no match | `references/style.md` | the shared `style.md` |
   | `[[setup]]` | no match | the `setup` skill | a link to `setup`'s `SKILL.md`, with the warning of rule 7 |
   | `[[x]]` | no match | no match | an error. A skill `x` in another plugin is never searched. |

4. A link with a path resolves relative to the linking file. Its result must
   still fall in a row the table allows.

5. An installed path is written relative to where the linking file lands in the
   pack. Every harness built for keeps a pack whole on install, so the path
   holds after install (section 9).

blocks.code:
.claude-plugin/packs/tools/
├── references/style.md          from SKILL.md: ../../references/style.md
└── skills/author/
    ├── SKILL.md                 the linking file lands here
    └── references/guide.md      from SKILL.md: references/guide.md

blocks.text:
6. A link to another component's note, or to a file in its folder, is rewritten
   to where that file lands in the same pack. The link text stays as written.
   From `skills/author/author.md`:

   | Source | Claude Code, Codex | Cursor, Pi (default naming) |
   |---|---|---|
   | `[[setup]]` | `[setup](../setup/SKILL.md)` | `[setup](../tools-setup/SKILL.md)` |
   | `[[setup#Usage]]` | `[setup](../setup/SKILL.md#Usage)` | `[setup](../tools-setup/SKILL.md#Usage)` |
   | `[[author]]` (its own note) | `[author](SKILL.md)` | `[author](SKILL.md)` |

   A fragment is kept. A component the harness's pack does not contain, such as an
   agent in any build or a command outside Claude Code, has no installed path.
   A link to it is an error for that harness.

7. A plain link to another skill's or command's note warns, naming the file
   and the link: `Did you mean to call /[[setup]]?`. The link still ships as a
   file link. A skill's link to its own note does not warn.

8. `/[[name]]` is a call (decision D3).
   - The `/` counts where it starts a line, or follows whitespace or one of
     `( " ' * > _ | [ =`. Anywhere else, such as `dir/[[x]]` or
     `[[A]]/[[B]]`, the `/` is text and `[[x]]` is an ordinary link.
   - A call to a skill renders as the string that runs it on that harness, in
     backticks. Nothing is copied. For the `setup` skill of plugin `tools`:

     | Harness | Default | With `naming: bare` (section 8 rule 6) |
     |---|---|---|
     | Claude Code | `` `/tools:setup` `` | same |
     | Codex | `` `$tools:setup` `` | same |
     | Cursor | `` `/tools-setup` `` | `` `/setup` `` |
     | Pi | `` `/skill:tools-setup` `` | `` `/skill:setup` `` |

   - A call with words keeps them: `/[[setup|the setup skill]]` renders as
     ``the setup skill (`/tools:setup`)``.
   - A fragment on a call, `/[[setup#Usage]]`, is an error, because a call
     cannot target a section. Link or embed the section instead.
   - The name is looked up among the marketplace's skills and commands
     (decision D2). A name found in no plugin of the marketplace is an error,
     even if another marketplace in the vault has it. A name two plugins
     share is an error that names both plugins. Rename one to fix it.
   - A call's result per target:

     | Call to | Claude Code | Codex, Cursor, Pi |
     |---|---|---|
     | a skill the pack contains | the call string above | the call string above |
     | a skill the pack does not contain (`targets`) | an error for that harness | an error for that harness |
     | a command | `` `/tools:deploy` `` | an error: their packs contain no commands |
     | an agent | an error: no pack contains agents | an error |
   - A call string written by hand in prose is an error that says to write
     `/[[setup]]`. One harness's form is wrong for the others. A string is
     checked in these steps:
     1. Take the call forms of every harness being built, with that
        harness's naming in effect for the plugin. For a command, take only
        the forms of harnesses whose packs contain commands.
     2. Keep only the forms that name the plugin. For the `setup` skill of
        plugin `tools`:

        | Form | Harness | Checked? |
        |---|---|---|
        | `/tools:setup` | Claude Code | Yes |
        | `$tools:setup` | Codex | Yes |
        | `/tools-setup` | Cursor, prefixed | Yes |
        | `/skill:tools-setup` | Pi, prefixed | Yes |
        | `/setup`, `/skill:setup` | Cursor or Pi with `naming: bare` | No. A bare name is too often other text, such as a path. |

     3. A form matches in prose when its sigil does not continue a word or
        path, and the character after it is not a letter `a` to `z`, a digit
        or `-`. So `/tools:setup-x` is not `/tools:setup`, and
        `/tools:setup.md` is.
     4. A match is an error. A match in a code span or fenced block is not
        checked and ships as written (rule 12).

     There is no escape form. To show a call string, put it in code.

9. `\/[[x]]` ships as the text `/[[x]]`. The leftover check of rule
   13 skips text an escape produced.

10. A link into a never-ship folder is refused with the same error in every
    link form.
11. A link to a missing file is an error that names the link.

12. Code is literal. Nothing inside a code span or fenced block is
    interpreted: no call, link or embed. A call written in code ships as
    written, so write calls in prose, where they render in backticks. There are
    two exceptions:

    | In code | Result |
    |---|---|
    | `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path>` | Rewritten (rule 15) |
    | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` | An error (rule 22) |

13. After the build, no unescaped `[[` may remain in prose.
    - Write `\[[` to keep the brackets as text: `\[[x]]` is not interpreted
      and ships as `[[x]]`.
    - A leftover `[[` is an error that names the file and the text.
    - Code spans and fenced blocks are not checked. Neither is text an escape
      produced.

14. Every error in this section names the linking file, the link as written and
    the rule it broke.

A component names a file of its plugin as `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path>`, such as
`${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool`. The build replaces the string with each
harness's own form (decision D9).

16. The path runs to the first character that cannot continue a path. A
    letter, digit, `.`, `_`, `-` or `/` continues it. A `.` at the end of the
    path is not part of it, so a full stop after a path is punctuation:

    | Text | Path |
    |---|---|
    | `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool.js --check` | `scripts/tool.js` |
    | `Run ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool.` | `scripts/tool` |

17. The path is a path in the plugin's pack, laid out as section 9 places
    files for Claude Code:

    | Path | Names |
    |---|---|
    | `scripts/tool` | the plugin's shared `scripts/tool` |
    | `skills/setup/scripts/run.sh` | the `setup` skill's `scripts/run.sh` |
    | `commands/deploy.md` | the `deploy` command's note |

    It must name a file the build ships. If it does not, the build fails. The
    error names the file holding the reference and the reference as written.

18. In Claude Code's pack it is written as `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path>`,
    which Claude Code expands in skill, command and agent text.

19. In Codex's, Cursor's and Pi's packs it is written as the path of that same file in that harness's pack, relative to the folder the text lands in. None of the three expands a variable in skill text. | Text lands in | `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool` becomes | |---|---| | `skills/review/SKILL.md` | `../../scripts/tool` | | `skills/review/references/guide.md` | `../../../scripts/tool` | | a file that embeds the text | the path from that file's folder | On Cursor and Pi, a path into a skill follows the skill's folder name there, `skills/

-/` by default (section 8 rule 6). Only the path is rewritten. The file it names is copied as is. How the path is used: | Harness | The path in skill text | Who resolves it | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/`, an absolute path once expanded | Claude Code | | Codex, Cursor, Pi | relative to the file it is written in | the model, before it uses the path | - The shell never reads `SKILL.md`. The model reads it and writes the command, so it turns the relative path into one it can run. - This holds for every relative path in skill text, to a reference or to a script, in the skill's own folders or the plugin's shared ones. A skill may run a plugin-shared script, such as `../../scripts/tool.js`. - The known risk: a model may paste the command as written. It then runs from the project folder, and the path does not resolve.

20. A path to a file the harness's pack does not contain is an error for that harness,
    the same as a link to it (rule 6). An example, in steps:
    1. `skills/review/review.md` contains
       `See ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/commands/deploy.md.`
    2. The Claude Code pack contains commands. It gets
       `See ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/commands/deploy.md.`
    3. The Codex pack has no `commands/` folder, because the Codex pack contains no
       commands.
    4. So the build fails for Codex. The error names `review.md` and
       `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/commands/deploy.md`.

21. `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` with no `/<path>` after it is an error in Markdown. It
    cannot be rewritten to a path for Codex, Cursor or Pi, and a vault writes
    one text for all harnesses.

22. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in interpreted text, code included, is an error
    that says to write `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`. Interpreted text is the files of rule
    15 (a component's note, the Markdown in its own and the plugin's
    `references/`, and text a note embed inlines) and `hooks/hooks.json`. A
    file that ships byte for byte, a never-ship folder and a container note's
    body are not checked. There is one syntax. To show Claude Code's variable

**What it is.** `build.out` in `skillwright.md`, or `--out` on the command

**Decided.** Both are dropped. Output always lands in `<root>/dist/<m>/`, such

own root copies it there, for example in CI.

- `bump --changed-since` uses its own temporary folder.

blocks.title: D2. The scope of a call

blocks.text: **What it is.** How far `/[[name]]` looks for the skill it calls.

**Decided.** A call looks across the whole marketplace. `/[[review]]` finds
`review` in any plugin of the marketplace. A name two plugins share is an
error that names both plugins; rename one. Links and embeds stay within the
plugin.
- A call copies no file, so it does not break containment.

- Calls across plugins are common, such as `/sdlc:task-work` from a `craft`
  skill. An own-plugin scope could not express them.

- The cost: a call can name a skill in a plugin the user did not install. The
  harness then reports an unknown command at run time.

blocks.title: D3. Calls and plain links to a skill

blocks.text: **What it is.** What `/[[setup]]` and `[[setup]]` mean when `setup` is a skill.

**Decided.** The syntax decides, not the target. v2 keeps the call and makes a
plain link a real link (section 4 rules 6 to 8).

- `/[[setup]]` is a call, with the `/` positions and the `\/[[` escape of
  section 4 rules 8 and 9. A call with words keeps them. A fragment on a call is an error.

- `[[setup]]` is a file link to the skill's installed `SKILL.md`, under the
  normal link scope (same plugin). `[[setup#Usage]]` links to that section.
- A skill's link to its own note is a file link to its own file.

- A plain link to another skill's or command's note warns
  `Did you mean to call /[[setup]]?`. A self-link does not warn.
- There is no mention form. Nothing renders a skill's name on its own.
- Code is literal, so a call in a code span is not interpreted.
**Why `/` and not `@`.**

- `/` matches how Claude Code runs a skill or command, `/name`, so the source
  reads like its output.

- Vaults written today already use it, so nothing has to be rewritten (see
  [v2-changes.md](v2-changes.md)).

- Its cost is the clash with paths, such as `dir/[[x]]`. The call-position
  rule handles that: a `/` inside a word or path is text.

- `@` was considered and rejected.
  - In Claude Code and Cursor it means mention or attach, `@file` or
    `@agent`, which is what a plain link already does.
  - It clashes with email addresses and GitHub `@user` mentions.
  - Every existing vault would have to be rewritten.

- Codex runs skills with `$` either way. The build writes each harness's own
  form from `/[[name]]`.

| `plugins/tools/hooks/hooks.json` | each harness's hooks file |
- The plugin folder already says where things go.

- `hooks/hooks.json` is the path Claude Code reads by default
  (harness-reference: `Claude Code Plugin manifest fields`).

- Keeping the lists would mean two settings with their own path checks, and
  `plugin: tools` would need a marketplace prefix to be unambiguous.
- The cost: a file shared by several plugins is copied into each.

- A file built from source outside the plugin no longer needs a copy rule.
  The author's build step writes it into the plugin's `scripts/`,
  `references/` or `assets/`, and skillwright copies it from there (section 3
  rule 16).

- A real consumer, the `sdlc` plugin, ships about 25 `assets:` entries from
  outside its vault to arbitrary pack paths. It fits this pattern (see the
  consumer note in [v2-changes.md](v2-changes.md)).
**What it is.** A list of globs in `skillwright.md` for files that never ship.

**Decided.** `build.exclude` is dropped. A file that must not ship goes in a
`docs/` folder, such as `skills/review/docs/notes.md`. `docs/` never ships.
- `docs/` already does the job, and the layout stays the only rule.

- An excluded file would also need an exemption from the folder rules of
  section 3, which refuse `notes.draft.md` beside `review.md`. That would be a
  second way to say what a folder may hold.

**What it is.** Whether `plugins/

/

.md` must exist.

**Decided.** The note is required. `plugins/tools/` with no `tools.md` is an
error that names the missing path. `init` writes the note.
- Every plugin has one file that holds its settings and its `version`.
- `bump` needs a note to write the version to.

- A note without a `version` still builds as `0.1.0`, with a warning
  (section 7 rule 7). The warning points at the one file to fix.

**What it is.** A plugin's MCP server configuration. Claude Code reads
`.mcp.json` at the plugin root (harness-reference: `Claude Code MCP config
file`). Claude Code, Codex and Cursor also read an `mcpServers` manifest field.

**Decided.** `.mcp.json` has no home in v2. A `.mcp.json` in a plugin folder
is an error that says so (section 3, "What a folder may hold"). It is not
skipped like other dot-named files. An MCP server kind comes later and writes
each harness's own file.

- A copied `.mcp.json` is right for Claude Code and may be wrong for the other
  harnesses, whose files and keys differ.

- A file that is right for one harness and wrong for others breaks installs
  quietly.
- Skipping it silently would break them quietly too, so it is an error.

blocks.title: D8. Embedding a file that is neither a note nor an image

blocks.text: **What it is.** `![[name]]` where the target is, say, a script or a CSV file.

**Decided.** A text file is inlined as a fenced code block (section 5 rules 9
to 14). With `scripts/run.sh` holding `echo hi`, `![[scripts/run.sh]]` ships as:

blocks.code:
```bash
echo hi
```

blocks.text:
- The info string comes from the extension: `.sh` gives `bash`, `.py` gives
  `python`, and an extension not in the table gives none.

- The fence is one backtick longer than the longest backtick run that starts a
  line in the file, and never fewer than three.

- The content is never escaped or changed. So a file with its own
  ```` ``` ```` block and `[[` text ships intact.
- Inside a list item, the block is indented to match the item.

- A binary file (not valid UTF-8) is refused. A fragment on a non-note file,
  `![[run.sh#main]]`, is refused.
- A plain `[[run.sh]]` stays a file link.
### D9. Plugin-root paths replace `build.launcher_path`

**What it is.** How a component or a hook names a file of its plugin, such as
a launcher script, so that the path works on every harness.

**Decided.** `build.launcher_path` is dropped and refused. Authors write
`${PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path>` (section 4 rules 15 to 26).

| Where | Source | Claude Code | Codex, Cursor, Pi |
|---|---|---|---|
| A skill's `SKILL.md`, prose or code | `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool` | `../../scripts/tool` |
| `hooks/hooks.json` | `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hook.sh` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hook.sh` | Codex `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/…`; Cursor and Pi no hooks (section 4 rule 23) |
- Every path is checked to name a file the pack ships.

- A path to a file in `scripts/`, `references/` or `assets/` is rewritten the
  same way, whether a skill's own or the plugin's shared copy. A path has one
  meaning, so it has one rule. The files themselves are copied as they are.

- `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` with no path after it is an error in Markdown. There is no
  path to rewrite it to for three harnesses.

- A target the harness's pack does not contain is an error for that harness, as a link
  to it is. A dead path breaks the skill at run time with no sign at build
  time.

- Hooks get each harness's own variable, and their paths are checked. A
  hook runs from the project folder, so a relative path would not resolve.

- `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in source is an error that says to write
  `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`. One syntax means one thing to search for and check.
- Scripts ship byte for byte. A script finds its own files relative to itself.

**Why a build-time string replacement.** No harness but Claude Code expands
a plugin-root variable in skill text, so the variable cannot be left for the
harness to fill in.

| Harness | Expands a plugin-root variable in skill text? | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | Yes, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` | `Claude Code Plugin root variable` |
| Cursor | No. Its variables expand only in `mcp.json`, and `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` is not one of them. Whether it sets `${CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT}` for hooks is not recorded either, so its pack ships no hooks (section 4 rule 23). | `Cursor Plugin root variable` |
| Codex | No. `PLUGIN_ROOT` is documented only for hooks. | |
| Pi | No | |

So the build replaces the string. Claude Code gets its own variable, and the
other harnesses get a relative path.
**Why `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`.**

- It is the open Agent Plugins standard's name (harness-reference:
  `Agent Plugins Plugin root variable`).

- It reads as the shell variable it becomes, so the source looks like a
  working command.

- It names no harness. The vault is written once for every harness, and its
  text should not favour one.

- It is the name Codex already uses for hooks, so on Codex a hook ships as
  written.

- Keeping `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` was rejected. It names one harness, and the
  source would read as if Claude Code were the target while three of four
  packs get something else.

- A template token such as `{{plugin}}` was rejected. It reads as neither a
  path nor a variable, it is close to the `{{harness}}` and `{{event}}` hook
  placeholders, and a source file using it is not runnable as written.

**The cost.** A code example that shows a shell `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`, such as
documentation of a Codex hook, is interpreted as a plugin-root path. It is
rewritten, or refused when it names no shipped file. The simplest fix needs no
new syntax: write the variable unbraced, `$PLUGIN_ROOT`. The shell reads it
the same way, and the build leaves it alone. So v2 has no escape form for it.
- Any plugin path works on every harness, not just one configured file.

- The plugin's folders are fixed, so the build knows where every file lands
  and can rewrite any path.

- The check turns a typo or a moved file into a build error instead of a
  failure at run time.
## Later

The layout is deliberately the recommended practice and nothing more. More
flexible structures may come in a later version of this spec.

These commands are out of v2 and may return in later milestones: `publish` to
a skills folder, `harness install`, `update`, `uninstall`, `link` and
`unlink`, `adopt`, `new`, `rename`, `move`, `build --watch`, and the other
current commands (`list`, `status`, `delete`, `convert`, `author`,
`unpublish`).

Build steps declared in `skillwright.md`, such as `build.before:`, may come
later. `build` would run them; `check` never would.

Richer hook authoring (hook notes) may come later; see
[#152](https://github.com/osdlc/skillwright/issues/152). v2 reads hooks only
from `hooks/hooks.json`. Hooks in the Cursor pack return when a probe confirms
that Cursor sets `${CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT}` for hook commands, tracked in the same
issue.
## Appendix A: Edge cases
Each case gives an input and the result.

1. **A component named `skillwright`.** A skill named `skillwright` has a note
   called `skillwright.md`. So the walk up from inside it meets a second
   `skillwright.md`. It is never taken for the root, because only the root
   has `marketplaces/` beside it.

blocks.code:
<root>/
├── skillwright.md                      the root file: marketplaces/ is beside it
└── marketplaces/acme/plugins/tools/
    └── skills/skillwright/
        └── skillwright.md              a skill's note: no marketplaces/ beside it

blocks.text:
The six structure names are reserved (section 3 rule 6), so a component
   named `marketplaces` cannot hold a `marketplaces/` folder.

   A whole vault copied inside another vault's tree is a different case. A
   walk up that starts inside the inner vault stops at the inner root, so the
   build reads the inner vault. A build started outside it reads only the
   outer root's `skillwright.md` and `marketplaces/` (section 1 rule 3). v2
   does not support nested vaults.

2. **A dot-named file a pack needs.**
   - Input: `assets/.eslintrc.json`.
   - Result: skipped. It does not ship, and there is no warning.
   - Fix: name it without the dot, and have the script or skill that uses it
     copy it to the dotted name.
   - `.mcp.json` in a plugin folder is the one dot-named file that is an
     error (decision D7).

3. **A link from a plugin's shared reference.**
   - Input: `plugins/tools/references/style.md` contains `[[guide]]`, and the
     plugin has `references/guide.md`.
   - Result: step 1 is skipped, since the file belongs to no component. Step
     2 searches the shared folders and component names. It finds
     `references/guide.md` and not `skills/author/references/guide.md`, which
     sits inside a component. It ships as `[guide](guide.md)`.

4. **A name that matches deep in a folder.**
   - Input: `[[layout]]`, with `references/design/layout.md` in the skill.
   - Result: it matches, at any depth. If `references/old/layout.md` also
     exists, it is an error that names both.

5. **A component left out by `targets`.**
   - Input: skill `deploy` sets `targets: [claude]`. Skill `review`, shipped
     everywhere, contains `/[[deploy]]`.
   - Result: Claude Code renders `` `/tools:deploy` ``. The build fails for
     Codex, Cursor and Pi, naming `review.md` and the call.
   - Fix: give `review` the same `targets`, or move the call out of it.

6. **A plugin and a marketplace with one name.**
   - Input: marketplace `osdlc` holds plugin `osdlc`.
   - Result: `bump osdlc` bumps the plugin. `bump --marketplace osdlc` bumps
     the marketplace.

7. **Two prefixed names that collide.**
   - Input: plugin `a-b` has skill `c`; plugin `a` has skill `b-c`.
   - Result: both are `a-b-c` on Cursor and Pi. That is an error for those
     harnesses, naming both. Claude Code and Codex are not affected.

8. **A never-ship name inside a shipped folder.**
   - Input: `skills/review/references/docs/x.md` and
     `plugins/tools/scripts/src/main.js`.
   - Result: both ship. `docs/` and `src/` are never-ship folders only
     directly in a plugin or component folder.

9. **`check` with no output yet.**
   - Input: a fresh clone with no `dist/`.
   - Result: `check` reports drift and exits 1. Run `build` first.

10. **A path at the end of a sentence.**
    - Input: `Run ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool.`
    - Result: the path is `scripts/tool`. The full stop stays as text.

11. **An indented fence in an embedded file.**
    - Input: `notes.txt` holds a line that starts with three spaces and
      ```` ``` ````.
    - Result: it counts. The embed's fence uses four backticks.

12. **A call in a container note.**
    - Input: the plugin note's body says `` Run `/[[setup]]` first. ``
    - Result: nothing. A container note's body is not interpreted and does
      not ship.

13. **Showing Claude Code's variable in a doc.**
    - Input: a code span `` `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/x` ``.
    - Result: an error. Write `` `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/x` `` instead.

14. **Malformed frontmatter in an embedded note.**
    - Input: `![[guide]]`, and `guide.md` opens with `---` but never closes
      it.
    - Result: an error that names `guide.md` and the embedding note.

15. **`naming` on a skill.**
    - Input: a skill note sets `pi: {naming: bare}`.
    - Result: refused. The error says to set it on the plugin.

blocks.title: Structure v2: what changes for v1 users (draft)

blocks.text:
What [[docs/spec/structure-v2|structure v2]] changes for a vault built with today's
tool (v1): the commands and features it removes, the decisions it amends, what
each of its decisions changes for an existing vault, and the one known
consumer migration. How v2 is built and tracked is in [[docs/spec/v2-plan|the plan]].
"Section" numbers refer to structure-v2.md.

v2 keeps `init`, `build`, `check` and `bump`. Every other command leaves v2
and may return in a later milestone:

| Command | Goes with it |
|---|---|
| `publish`, `unpublish` | `build.destinations` |
| `harness install`, `update`, `uninstall`, `link`, `unlink` | |
| `adopt` | `--from`, `--from-git`, `build.scan_locations` |
| `new`, `rename`, `move`, `delete`, `convert` | |
| `build --watch` | |
| `list`, `status`, `author` | |

A removed command is now an unknown command: a usage error, exit 3, with no
hint that it was removed.
These flags go too:

| Flag | Why | |---|---| | `--config` | `--vault` names the root. | | `--namespace` | `build.namespace` is gone. | | `--out` | Output is fixed at `dist//` (D1). | | `--skills-root` | Only `marketplaces/` is read. | | `--watch` | `build --watch` is out of v2. | | `init --out`, `init --name` | `init` takes `

` (section 10 rule 1). |

`--vault`, `--marketplace`, `--json`, `--quiet`, `--dry-run` and `--yes` stay
(section 10 rule 5). `build` and `bump` still ask before writing, so `--yes`
is still needed off a terminal.

blocks.title: The root and the root file

blocks.text: - A vault with no root file, read with every default.

- The walk-up for the nearest `skillwright.md`, and its reserved-name rule
  (`reserved-name`). The walk-up stays, but it now stops only at a folder
  that holds both `skillwright.md` and `marketplaces/` (section 1 rule 2).
- `--config`. `--vault` names the root.

- The root file as a marketplace. Its marketplace fields move to
  `marketplaces/<m>/<m>.md`.

- `workspace: true`, and `marketplaces/<m>/skillwright.md` as a member file.
  There is one root file, and every marketplace sits under it.

- The `name` key on any note. The folder name is the name, and a `name` key is
  refused.

- `build.namespace` and prefixed keys (`sw-version`, an `sw:` block). A
  prefixed key is now an unknown key.

- A root `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` or `hooks/` as a plugin named after
  the marketplace, and the root file's `version` as that plugin's version.
- A root `plugins/` as the plugins of a single marketplace.
- Marketplaces below the top, and components promoted to a marketplace.
- Flat entry notes (`skills/x.md`) and `SKILL.md` entries.
- Optional plugin notes (decision D6).
- `build.patterns` and every custom folder glob.
- `build.exclude` (decision D5). A file that must not ship goes in `docs/`.

- Obsidian's "Excluded files" (`userIgnoreFilters` in `.obsidian/app.json`).
  `.obsidian/` is never read, so a skill listed there now builds.

- Loose files in a component folder. Each folder now holds only the entries
  its row in section 3's "What a folder may hold" table lists. Anything else
  is an error.

- New: six reserved names (`marketplaces`, `plugins`, `skills`, `agents`,
  `commands`, `hooks`) for any marketplace, plugin or component.

- New: a `.mcp.json` in a plugin folder is an error (decision D7), not a
  shipped asset.

- New: the body of `.md` and `

.md` is not interpreted and does not ship.

- Hook notes, `hooks/<h>/<h>.md`. Hooks come only from `hooks/hooks.json`. A
  folder or any other file in `hooks/` is an error.

- `build.out`, `--out` and the "no default output" rule. Output is fixed at
  `dist/<m>/`.

- `<harness>: {packs: <path>}`, with its overlap checks and the
  `stale-output` warning.
- `build.assets` and `build.hooks` (decision D4).

- The plugin `assets/` folder copied flat to the pack root (`assets/bin/tool`
  shipping as `bin/tool`). A plugin's `assets/` now ships as `assets/`. The
  launcher moves to `scripts/`.

- Bare skill names as Cursor's default. Cursor now writes a plugin's skill as `

-`, folder and `name`, as Pi already does. `cursor: {naming: bare}` keeps today's plain names (section 8 rule 6). A call to a Cursor skill renders `/

-`, not `/`.

- `targets` values other than `claude`, `codex`, `cursor` and `pi`. The
  publish targets (`amp`, `antigravity`, `copilot`, `opencode`, `portable`)
  and the aliases (`claude-code`, `codex-cli`, `github-copilot`) are now
  refused (section 9 rule 12).

- Hooks in the Cursor pack. The build now leaves them out and warns, until a
  probe confirms that Cursor sets `${CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT}` for hook commands
  (section 4 rule 23, [#152](https://github.com/osdlc/skillwright/issues/152)).
- New: `check` with no `dist/<m>/` reports drift (exit 1).

- New: `build` with no `--marketplace` builds every marketplace. The working
  directory no longer picks one.

| v1 | v2 |
|---|---|
| A plain `[[skill]]` rendered the skill's name (a mention). | An ordinary file link that warns `Did you mean to call /[[skill]]?` (D3). |
| A link resolved vault-wide: a basename match across the vault, the `own_folder_candidate` tiebreak, and `link-ambiguous` across folders. | It resolves within the plugin in two steps (section 4 rule 3). |
| A linked file from anywhere was copied to `references/vault/` or `assets/vault/`. | Every reachable file already ships, so nothing is copied for a link. |
| An embed or link to nothing was reported, and its words shipped. | An error (section 4 rule 11). |
| An embed of a file that is neither a note nor an image became a plain link. | A text file is inlined as a fenced code block (D8). |
| Calls inside code spans and fenced blocks were interpreted. | Code is literal (section 4 rule 12). |
| A fragment on a call or a mention was checked and then dropped. | On a call, `/[[setup#Usage]]`, an error. On a plain link it is kept. |
| A note with malformed frontmatter embedded its body. | An error that names both notes (section 5 rule 4). |
| A hand-written call string was refused in prose and code, including a bare `/setup` for a skill of the note's own plugin. `\/tools:setup` kept it as text. | Refused in prose only, in the four forms that name the plugin (section 4 rule 8). A bare `/setup` is not checked. In code it ships as written, and there is no escape form. |
| `\[[x]]` shipped with its backslash, as `\[[x]]`. | It ships as `[[x]]`: the backslash is removed (section 4 rule 13). |
| Two skills sharing a called name: `skill-call-ambiguous`, with the path of the one meant as the fix. | An error that names both plugins. There is no path form of a call; rename one. |

- `build.launcher_path` (decision D9). Authors now write
  `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path>`. Every such path in a component's Markdown is
  checked and replaced, not one configured path. A path that names nothing
  shipped, left as written in v1, is now an error.

- `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` as the source form, in notes and in hooks files. It
  is now an error that says to write `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` (decision D9).

| Decision | Amendment |
|---|---|
| [[docs/decisions/D-WNTQ-harness-profile-values-from-config|D-WNTQ]] | `pi: {naming}` stays settable, `cursor: {naming}` is added, and `packs` is not settable. |
| [[docs/decisions/D-KVMB-bare-keys-by-default|D-KVMB]] | `build.namespace` and prefixed keys are gone. An unknown key still warns, with two exceptions: the removed keys `workspace` (root file) and `packs` (harness block) are refused. A key the table lists is refused where it does not belong: a key that is not inherited in the root file, `name` on any note, `build:` outside the root file, and the removed `build:` keys. |
| [[docs/decisions/D-GPYR-convention-first|D-GPYR]] | Its patterns layer is gone. |

Each decision's rule is in section 12. This part says what v1 does and what
an existing vault must change.
v1 requires it. The repo's own `plugin/` builds beside its root file:

blocks.code:
build:
  out: .        # writes plugin/.claude-plugin/, plugin/.agents/, ...

blocks.text: Existing vaults:
1. Remove `out:`.

2. The repo's `plugin/` built trees move from `plugin/.claude-plugin/` and its
   siblings to `plugin/dist/osdlc/`.

3. The `plugin` workflow diffs that folder, and `plugin-release` copies from
   it.

blocks.title: D2. The scope of a call

blocks.text:
v1 looks a called name up across the whole vault. The repo's `author` skill
calls `/[[setup]]` in its own plugin, `skillwright`:

| Harness | Renders as |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `/skillwright:setup` |
| Codex | `$skillwright:setup` |
| Pi | `/skill:skillwright-setup` |

If two skills share the name, v1 stops with `skill-call-ambiguous` and asks for
the path of the one meant.

Existing vaults: none, unless a call names a skill in another marketplace of
the same vault. That call is now an error.

blocks.title: D3. Calls and plain links to a skill

blocks.text: v1 has two forms:

| Source | v1 renders | Runs the skill? |
|---|---|---|
| `/[[setup]]` | `/skillwright:setup` on Claude Code | Yes: a call |
| `[[setup]]` | `skillwright:setup`, the skill's name | No: a mention |

A skill's link to its own note ships as a file link, `[setup](SKILL.md)`
([#53](https://github.com/osdlc/skillwright/issues/53) asked for the name).
v1 also interprets calls inside code spans and fenced blocks. v1 vaults
already write calls as `/[[name]]`, which is one reason v2 keeps the `/`.
Existing vaults:

1. A v1 mention, `[[name]]`, now ships as a file link and warns. Write
   `/[[name]]` if a call was meant, or keep the link.

2. A call inside a code span or fenced block now ships as written. Move it
   into prose.

3. The repo's `plugin/` has 10 calls, all `/[[...]]`:

   | Where | Count | Change |
   |---|---|---|
   | Heading self-calls, such as `# /[[author]]` | 3 | None: they are in prose. |
   | Code spans in skill notes, such as `` `/[[setup]]` `` | 6 | Move into prose, keeping the `/`. A call renders in backticks, so the output is the same. |
   | The plugin note's body | 1 | None: a container note's body is not interpreted and does not ship. |

4. The `author` skill's "Links" section
   (`plugins/skillwright/skills/author/author.md`, lines 57 to 75) is
   rewritten to describe v2. That includes its last bullet, v1's vault-wide
   `link-ambiguous` rule. Its syntax examples stay in code and ship as
   written.

`LICENSE` lands at the root of the `tools` pack. `hooks.json` is translated
into each harness's hooks file.
Existing vaults:
1. Move each file into its plugin.

2. A built file is written there by the author's build step, with its source
   in `src/` or outside the vault.
3. The `sdlc` plugin uses `build.assets`; see "Consumer migration" below.

blocks.code:
build:
  exclude: ["**/*.draft.md"]

blocks.text: `skills/review/notes.draft.md` stays in the vault and is not shipped.

Existing vaults: move excluded files into `docs/`. The repo's `plugin/` uses
no `exclude`.

v1 builds a plugin folder without a note. Its name is the folder's name, and
its version is `0.1.0` with a warning.

Existing vaults: add a note to any plugin without one. The repo's `plugin/`
already has `plugins/skillwright/skillwright.md`.

v1 has no MCP kind. An author ships the file through the flat assets copy:
`plugins/tools/assets/.mcp.json` lands at `<pack>/.mcp.json` for every
harness.

Existing vaults: remove the `.mcp.json`, or keep the plugin on v1 until the
MCP kind lands. The repo's `plugin/` has none.

blocks.title: D8. Embedding a file that is neither a note nor an image

blocks.text:
v1 ships `![[run.sh]]` as a plain link, `[run.sh](scripts/run.sh)`, and copies
the file. The `!` changes nothing.
Existing vaults:

1. An `![[file]]` of a text file that shipped as a link now ships the file's
   text. Write `[[file]]` to keep the link.
2. An embed of a binary file is now refused.
3. The repo's `plugin/` has none.
v1, in steps:

1. `build.launcher_path` names one launcher, such as `bin/tool`, shipped
   through the flat assets copy.

2. A skill calls it as `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/tool`. Claude Code keeps the
   call.

3. For Codex, Cursor and Pi, the build rewrites that one path to
   `../../bin/tool`, relative to the skill's folder.

4. Any other `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/...` path is left as written. That is dead
   text on those three harnesses.

5. If the plugin does not ship the launcher, the call is also left as written,
   with no warning.

6. On Pi, a separate step renames `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/` to `skills/

-`, but keeps the variable, which Pi does not expand.

7. A Markdown file in a skill's `references/` is rewritten relative to the
   skill's folder, not its own, so its `../..` is one level short.

8. Hooks write `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, swapped for each harness's own
   variable. v2 keeps the swap, with `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` as the source. The

| `[t](https://x.io)`, `<https://x.io>`, `[t](mailto:a@b)` | shipped as written, not checked |
| `[t](#usage)` | shipped as written, not checked |
Plain links:

- `[[setup]]` from `author` renders as `[setup](../setup/SKILL.md)` on Claude
  Code and `[setup](../tools-setup/SKILL.md)` on Cursor and Pi, and warns
  `Did you mean to call /[[setup]]?`.
- `[[setup#Usage]]` keeps its fragment.
- A skill's link to its own note is `[author](SKILL.md)`, with no warning.

- A link to a command is a file link on Claude Code and fails the build for
  Codex, Cursor and Pi. A link to an agent fails the build.
Calls:

| Source | Claude Code | Codex | Cursor | Pi |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/[[setup]]` | `` `/tools:setup` `` | `` `$tools:setup` `` | `` `/tools-setup` `` | `` `/skill:tools-setup` `` |
| `/[[setup]]`, `naming: bare` | same | same | `` `/setup` `` | `` `/skill:setup` `` |
| `/[[setup\|words]]` | ``words (`/tools:setup`)`` | ``words (`$tools:setup`)`` | ``words (`/tools-setup`)`` | ``words (`/skill:tools-setup`)`` |
| `/[[deploy]]`, a command | `` `/tools:deploy` `` | error | error | error |
| `/[[helper]]`, an agent | error | error | error | error |
| `/[[deploy]]`, `deploy` with `targets: [claude]` (Appendix A5) | `` `/tools:deploy` `` | error naming the file and the call | the same | the same |
Also:
- `/[[setup#Usage]]` is an error.

- `/[[review]]` finds a skill in another plugin; a name two plugins share is
  an error naming both plugins. A name found only in another marketplace is
  an error.

- A `/` that starts a line, or follows whitespace or one of
  `( " ' * > _ | [ =`, starts a call: one test per character.
- `dir/[[x]]` is a link, not a call. In `[[A]]/[[B]]`, `[[B]]` is a link.

- `` `/[[x]]` `` in a code span ships as written. `\/[[x]]` ships as
  `/[[x]]` and passes the leftover check.
- A call in a container note's body does nothing (Appendix A12).
Hand-written calls (section 4 rule 8):

| In prose | Result |
|---|---|
| `/tools:setup`, `$tools:setup`, `/tools-setup`, `/skill:tools-setup` | an error that says to write `/[[setup]]`, one test per form |
| `/tools:deploy`, a command | the same error |
| `/setup`, `/skill:setup` | shipped as written |
| `/tools:setup-x` | shipped as written: the match must end before a character outside `a-z`, `0-9` and `-` |
| `/tools:setup.md`, `/tools:setup,` | the error |
| `$tools:deploy`, `/tools-deploy`, a command | shipped as written: Codex and Cursor packs contain no commands |
| `/tools-setup` with `cursor: {naming: bare}` | shipped as written: that is not Cursor's form then |
| `/tools-setup` with `build.harnesses: [claude]` | shipped as written: Cursor is not built |
| any of the forms in a code span or fenced block | shipped as written |
| `\/tools:setup` | not an escape; the same error |
| `a/tools:setup`, `x$tools:setup` | not a call: the sigil continues a word or path |
Code and leftovers:

- `[[x]]`, `/[[x]]` and `![[x]]` in a code span or fenced block ship as
  written.

- `\[[x]]` in prose ships as `[[x]]`, and `\/[[x]]` ships as `/[[x]]`. Today's
  code keeps the backslash in `\[[x]]`, so this commit changes it.
- A leftover `[[` in prose is refused. One in code or after `\` is not.
Embeds:
- The worked example of section 5 ships as shown.
- A heading embed inlines the section with its subsections.
- A block embed inlines the block without its marker.
- A missing heading is `fragment-unresolved`.
- A nested embed's link is written relative to the outer file.

- A cycle prints its loop. A note that embeds itself is a cycle. Two embeds
  of different sections of one note are not.

- A call inside embedded text renders as it would in place (section 5 rule
  19).

- An embedded note's frontmatter is dropped. Malformed frontmatter is an error
  naming both notes.
- An embed of a missing file is an error naming the embed (section 5 rule 3).

- Inlined text is trimmed of leading and trailing blank lines (section 5
  rule 8).
- An image embed is an image link.

- `![[run.sh]]` ships as a `bash` fenced block. An unknown extension gets no
  info string.

- A file holding its own ```` ``` ```` block and `[[` text is fenced with four
  backticks and ships byte for byte, with its `[[` not interpreted. So is a
  file whose fence is indented three spaces.
- An embed inside a list item is indented to the item.

- A binary file is refused. `![[run.sh#main]]` is refused. `[[run.sh]]` is a
  link.
Plugin-root paths (D9):

| Source | Claude Code | Codex, Cursor, Pi |
|---|---|---|
| `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool` in a skill's prose or code span | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool` | `../../scripts/tool` |
| the same, from the skill's `references/guide.md` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool` | `../../../scripts/tool` |
| the same, from the plugin's shared `references/style.md` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool` | `../scripts/tool` |
| `Run ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool.` | path `scripts/tool`, full stop kept | the same |
| `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/commands/deploy.md` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/commands/deploy.md` | error |
| `$PLUGIN_ROOT/x` | as written | as written |
Also:

- A path into another skill follows `skills/

-/` on Cursor and Pi.
- `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool.js` is not `scripts/tool`.
- A path naming nothing shipped fails, naming the file and the reference.

- A lone `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` in Markdown is an error. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in
  a note or a code span is an error that says to write `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`. In a
  file under `docs/`, or in a plugin note's body, it is not checked.
- A plain `scripts/x.py` in a `SKILL.md` ships as written and is not checked.
- An embedded reference is written from the embedding file.
- A script in `scripts/` holding the variable ships byte for byte.

- `![[run.sh]]`, where `run.sh` holds `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tool`, a lone
  `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` and a `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, inlines the file unchanged
  with no error.

- A hook command's `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/missing.sh` fails the build. A
  lone `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` in a hook is allowed.

The repo's `plugin/`: code is now literal, so the six `/[[...]]` calls in
code spans in the skill notes move into prose, keeping the `/`
(`` `/[[setup]]` `` becomes `/[[setup]]`). The output is the same. The three
heading self-calls, such as `# /[[author]]`, stay. The plugin note's
`` `/[[setup]]` `` stays too: a container note's body is not read.

blocks.title: 6. Docs and the repo's plugin skills

blocks.text: Changes:

1. The reference docs: `docs/reference/skillwright-md.md` is rewritten; its
   Patterns, Several marketplaces and Publishing one note by path sections
   go. `docs/reference/fields.md` is already current from the commits that
   changed the key table.

2. The CLI README's verb and option tables shrink to the four commands. Its
   Configuration section is rewritten.
3. `packages/ts/tradecraft-wasm/README.md` lists the remaining exports.

4. `plugin/README.md` describes the v2 layout, `plugin/dist/osdlc/` and the
   v2 build commands. `plugin/skillwright.md`'s body drops `--config`.

5. `docs/guide/getting-started.md` (today `init --out`, `list`, `publish`,
   `harness install`) and `site/index.html` (today `publish`, `list`,

6. `docs/terms/`: the entries for removed ideas (`destination`,
   `destination-manifest`, `rail`, `adopt`, `namespace`) go or are rewritten,

7. The decisions v2 amends, `docs/decisions/D-WNTQ-*`, `D-KVMB-*` and
   `D-GPYR-*`, are edited in place to match v2 (the amendments in
   v2-changes.md).

8. The plugin's skills are rewritten for v2 (the table in "The repo's own
   `plugin/`"). The `publish` skill is dropped. The `author` skill's syntax
   examples stay in code, where they ship as written, except plugin-root
   paths: rule 25 interprets `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/…` in code, and rule 22 refuses
   `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, so those examples are written unbraced,
   `$PLUGIN_ROOT` and `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`.
Tests first:

- A test over the plugin's source notes: no note names a removed command or
  flag (`publish`, `status`, `list`, `adopt`, `harness`, `--config`, `--out`,
  `--namespace` and the rest of v2-changes.md's lists) outside a line that
  says it is gone.

- Every `/[[...]]` call in `author` and `setup` resolves: the build of
  `plugin/` succeeds with no warning, and `/[[publish]]` appears nowhere.

- The `plugin` workflow's drift check passes on the rebuilt
  `plugin/dist/osdlc/`.
The PR is done when all of these hold:
- [ ] Every gate under "The gates" passes on every commit.

- [ ] Every numbered rule in the spec, and every case in its Appendix A, is
      covered by at least one test.

- [ ] `plugin/` is in the v2 layout and builds to `plugin/dist/osdlc/`, and
      the `plugin` workflow's drift check passes.

- [ ] `docs/reference/skillwright-md.md`, `docs/reference/fields.md`, the CLI
      README, the wasm package README, `tradecraft-core/README.md`,
      `docs/guide/getting-started.md`, `site/index.html`, `docs/terms/` and
      `plugin/skillwright.md`'s body describe v2.
- [ ] D-WNTQ, D-KVMB and D-GPYR are edited in place to match v2.

This inventory is a starting map of where v2 touches the code, read at
`2d11033c` (`origin/main` after
[#143](https://github.com/osdlc/skillwright/pull/143)), with paths under
`packages/rust/` unless they start at the repository root. It is not a set of
instructions: the implementor decides how, as long as the commit order, the
tests and the gates above hold. The number in brackets is the commit.

- `paths.rs` [2]:
  - Go: `find_root_file`, `is_component_note`, `is_reserved_note`,
    `is_vault_root_file`, `is_marketplace_entry`, `is_flat_root_file_name`,
    `workspace_above`, `RootRead`, `read_workspace_above`, `workspace_file`,
    `read_root`, `read_root_both`.
  - Change: the walk-up now stops at a folder holding both `skillwright.md`
    and `marketplaces/`.
  - `marketplace_inputs` and `load_marketplace` become one loader, in steps:
    read the root file, list `marketplaces/*/`, read each `<m>.md`.

- `patterns.rs` [2]: almost all of it goes.
  - Go: `Patterns::canonical`, `plugin_folder`, `assets_folder`,
    `sibling_files`, `source_folders`, `warnings`, `warnings_with`,
    `keep_conventional`, `workspace_exclude_warnings`, and with D5 the exclude
    list and the glob matcher (`glob_match`, `glob_problem`).
  - Stays: the never-ship rule, which can move into `discover.rs`. It now
    applies only directly in a plugin or component folder.

- `settings.rs`:
  - Go: `FolderPatterns`, `folder_patterns`, `globs`, `warn_nested` [2];
    `DestinationSetting` and the `destinations` and `scan_locations` keys
    [1]; the `patterns` and `out` keys [2]; `namespace` [3]; `AssetSetting`
    and `HookSetting` (D4) and `launcher_path` [4]. Each removed key joins the
    refused list in its commit.
  - Change [3]: `RootFile::inherit` becomes the root-defaults step of the
    cascade. `compose_root_file` writes a root with no marketplace fields.
    `root_file_config` and `RootFile::to_config` shrink. An unknown root-file
    key warns. A key that is not inherited, and `workspace`, are refused.
  - Change [2]: `MarketplaceFields` is read from `<m>.md`, not the root file.

- `namespace.rs` [3]: the prefixed stem goes, with `InvalidStem` and
  `StemProblem`. Either delete `Namespace` and its parameter everywhere, or
  keep only `Namespace::bare()`. It is threaded through `discover.rs`,
  `export.rs`, `frontmatter.rs`, `keys.rs`, `paths.rs`, `source_view.rs`,
  `vault.rs`, `model/`, `harness/translator.rs` and `lib.rs`'s re-exports.

- `frontmatter.rs` [3]: the prefixed-namespace reading goes: the flat and
  nested shapes and the `mixed-frontmatter-shape` refusal. A `name` key is
  refused with "delete it".

- `keys.rs`: the `Hook` rows, which describe hook-note frontmatter, go [2].
  The `name` row becomes a refusal [3]. `ADOPTABLE` goes [1].

- `projection.rs`: stays; `harness/translator.rs` renders through it. Parts
  only removed commands use go [1]: `content_hash` (adopt) and `file_hash`
  (publish).

- `discover.rs` [2]:
  - `classify` becomes a fixed-depth match.
  - Go: `conventional`, `folder_placement_with`, `RESERVED_NAME_REASON`,
    `SKILL_ENTRY`, `is_skill_entry`, the `SKILL.md` branch of `is_entry`, and
    `placement`'s `container_level` (promoted components).
  - `container_notes`, `container_notes_with` and `read_container` read fixed
    paths.
  - `under_a_kind_folder` and `refuse_stray` turn into the layout check of
    section 11.
  - New: the six reserved names, the per-folder entry table, and the
    `.mcp.json` error.

- `model/cascade.rs`:
  - Go [2]: `only_marketplace`, `sole_marketplace`, `marketplaces_in`, and
    the "a note under no marketplace takes the one marketplace" rule.
  - [2]: `marketplace_note` reads `<m>.md`. `belongs_to` becomes a path
    prefix test.
  - New [3]: a marketplace with no `version` writes no version and no
    warning.

- `model/load.rs`:
  - Go or shrink [2]: `standalone` (publish of one note), `members_folder`,
    `has_folder`, the marketplace's-own-plugin branch of `missing_versions`,
    the loading of hook notes (`hooks/<h>/<h>.md`), and `plugin_folder`.
  - Go [4]: `load_assets`, `load_hook_files` (D4), `folder_assets` (the flat
    copy; replaced by copying the three shared folders under their own
    names), `asset_covers` (its last use was the launcher check).
  - Go [4]: the `plugin.launcher` set from `build.launcher_path`, which only
    `asset_covers` fills.
  - [2]: `marketplace_name` and `resolve_marketplace` read the folder.
    Container note bodies are no longer read.
  - `apply_naming` already fills `bare_on` and `prefixed_on` from the
    `cursor` and `pi` blocks; it needs no change. New [4]: a `naming` key on
    a component is refused, saying to set it on the plugin.

- `source_view.rs` [2, 4]: the workspace folding in `effective_config`,
  `effective_configs`, `marketplace_folder` and `marketplace_notes` goes [2].
  `output_overlaps_vault`, `output_in`, `output_paths` and
  `check_pack_location` go [4]. Output cannot overlap source when only
  `marketplaces/` is read.

- `compile.rs` [5]:
  - Resolution: `CompileSource::resolve` changes from vault-wide to the two
    steps of section 4 rule 3. A file with no component starts at step 2. A
    shared file lands at the pack root, and its link is written relative to
    where the linking file lands. `own_folder_candidate` and the
    `references/vault/` and `assets/vault/` placements go.
    `vault_link_index` indexes one plugin, not the vault.
  - Containment: a real-path check is added beside `refuse_never_shipped`.
  - Calls (D3): `TokenKind::Call`, `TokenKind::Escape` (`\/[[`), `sigil_at`,
    `replace_call`, `render_call` and `format_call` stay. The call positions
    no longer include a backtick. `check_call_fragment` turns from "checked,
    then dropped" into an error. The call index (`skill_index` in
    `model/load.rs`) adds commands for harnesses whose packs contain them.
  - Plain links: `skill_mention` and the `mention` path of `render_or_mark`
    go. A plain link to a skill is a file link, plus the new "Did you mean to
    call" warning.
  - Code is literal: `scan_code_calls`, `code_token`, `TokenKind::Unconverted`
    with its `unconverted-call` warning, and the in-code branch of
    `format_call` go.
  - Leftovers: `validate_no_obsidian_syntax` skips code spans, fenced blocks,
    `\[[`-escaped text and text a `\/[[` escape produced.
  - Hand-written calls: `literal_skill_calls` and `literal-skill-call` stay,
    with three changes. They skip code spans and fenced blocks. The
    `LiteralForm::Bare` form (`/skill`, for the note's own plugin) goes, and a
    `/p-s` form for Cursor is added. The `\/` and `\$` escape goes. The
    error says to write `/[[name]]`.
  - Missing targets: in `replace_token`, an embed or link to nothing becomes
    an error instead of an entry in `unresolved`.
  - Embeds: a non-note, non-image embed is inlined as a fenced block (D8).
    New code: the extension table, the fence length (counting fences indented
    up to three spaces), list indentation and the UTF-8 check. Malformed
    frontmatter in an embedded note becomes an error. Embed expansion,
    `select_fragment` and the cycle check stay.

- `harness/profile.rs` [4]:
  - `PluginFormat::packs` stays a fixed value. `owned_paths_at` and the config
    override path go.
  - The Cursor row: `naming` changes from `Source::Knowledge` to
    `Source::Constant(SkillNaming::PluginPrefixed)`, as the Pi row's is, with
    a comment saying why (see "Settled and open"). `naming_choice` is already
    `true`. The test that checks each row's naming against harness knowledge
    (`skills/plugin-namespace`) then treats Cursor like Pi.
  - The Cursor row: `carries_hooks` becomes `false` and
    `hooks_manifest_entry` becomes `None`. The build warns once per plugin
    with a `hooks/hooks.json`.
  - `CliInvocation` stays as the per-harness switch, now for every
    plugin-root path (D9) [5].

- `harness/translator.rs` and `harness/manifest.rs`:
  - `naming_of` and `plugin_block` need no change: the block already starts
    from the marketplace's, which holds the root file's defaults, and
    overlays the plugin's.
  - `refuse_prefixed_collisions` already refuses every duplicate, bare ones
    too, where the profile's default prefixes. With Cursor's default changed,
    it covers Cursor with no new code. Its 64-character check does too.

- `model/mod.rs` and `harness/translator.rs` (D9): - `Segment::LauncherCall`, `push_text`'s one-path split and `rewrite_launcher_calls` go [4]. - New [5]: a plugin-root path segment that holds any path after `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/`, checked against the files the pack ships. A trailing `.` is not part of the path. - A source `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and a lone `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` are refused there. - `write_body` writes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/` for Claude Code. For the other harnesses it writes the path relative to the folder the text lands in, so a resource under `references/` gets its own depth, not the skill's. - `rewrite_sibling_paths` goes: Pi's `skills/

-/` folder is where the rewrite lands. `relative_path` stays.

- `hooks_file.rs` [4, 5]: `localize`, the variable swap, stays. Its
  `CANONICAL_ROOT` becomes `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`, and a source
  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is refused [4]. It gains the path check [5].

- `export.rs` [2, 4]: the CLI passes `<root>/dist/<m>/` as
  `ExportRequest::out_root` [2], and `out_root` goes [4]. The
  `stale-output` warning, moved-packs handling, `MarketplaceConfig::launcher_path`
  and the launcher tests go [4]; their cases become commit 5's plugin-root
  path tests.

- `walk.rs` and `discover.rs` [2]: `walk::excluded_files` and its use in
  `discover.rs` go, with the `userIgnoreFilters` tests, and
  `markdown_vault_fs::hide` where only that filter uses it.
- `vault.rs` [2]: `bundle_root` keeps only the `<name>/<name>.md` shape.

- `tradecraft-core/src/publish.rs`:
  - Go: everything that writes to a destination: `publish_skill`'s
    single-note arms, the destination manifest, the rails, `publishes_to`,
    `overrides_for`, `override_states` and `accepted_override_keys`.
  - Stay, because `export.rs` and `model/cascade.rs` call them: the plugin
    arm, `plugin_format_carries_commands`, `plugin_format_carries_hooks`,
    `kind_has_renderer`, `canonical_target`, `KNOWN_TARGETS` and
    `accepted_keys`. `KNOWN_TARGETS` and `canonical_target` shrink to
    `claude`, `codex`, `cursor` and `pi` in commit 3, with no aliases. Moving those into `export.rs` or `harness/` is a

- `tradecraft-core/src/guard.rs`, the rails: the publish-only rails go [1].

  `export.rs` calls (`assert_destination_allowed`,
  `assert_destination_allowed_for_vault`) go when output is fixed at
  `dist/<m>/` [2], since output can no longer land in the source.

- `tradecraft-core/src/status.rs`: `status_of` and `units_depending_on` go.

- `tradecraft-core/src/authoring.rs`: all of it.

- `tradecraft-core/src/adopt.rs`: `adopt_skills`, `AdoptRequest`,

- `tradecraft-core/src/scan.rs`: `scan_roots`, `scan_root` and

- `skillwright/src/commands/`: `publish.rs`, `status.rs`, `list.rs`,

- `skillwright/src/apply.rs` (the authoring writer), `git_source.rs` and

- `skillwright/src/cli.rs`: every command but `init`, `build`, `check` and

- `skillwright/Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`: dependencies only the removed

- `tradecraft-wasm/src/lib.rs`: `publishSkill`, `adoptSkills`, `statusOf`
  and `publishableKinds` go. `exportSkills`, `discoverComponents`,
  `loadMarketplace`, `parseRootFile`, `rootFileConfig`, `knownTargets` and
  `canonicalTarget` stay. `validateNamespace` goes in commit 3.
  `src/core.ts`'s hand-kept `Target` union shrinks to the four names in
  commit 3.

- `packages/ts/tradecraft-wasm` (repository root): the wrappers in
  `src/core.ts` and the re-exports in `src/index.ts` for those exports,
  `tests/status-of.test.ts` and `examples/publish-a-skill.test.ts`.
  `InvalidNamespaceError` and `validateNamespace` go in commit 3.

- Examples: `tradecraft-core/examples/publish.rs` and
  `skillwright/examples/list.rs`. `cargo clippy --all-targets` builds them,

- Tests, deleted:
  - `skillwright/tests/`: `authoring.rs`, `author.rs`, `harness.rs`,

  - The publish, status, list, adopt and authoring cases in
    `skillwright/tests/cli.rs` and `consumer_flows.rs`.
  - The publish, adopt and status cases in
    `tradecraft-core/tests/release_api.rs`, and the constructors of removed
    types in `tradecraft-core/tests/constructors.rs`.

- `resolve.rs` [2]:
  - `resolve_run` keeps a walk-up, but one that stops at a folder holding both
    `skillwright.md` and `marketplaces/`. It loses `--config`,
    `--skills-root` and the workspace fold.
  - `workspace_runs`, `refuse_workspace`, `workspace_warnings`,
    `member_workspace_warnings`, `is_workspace`, `configured_out` and
    `resolve_skills_root` go or shrink to "every marketplace, or the one
    `--marketplace` names". The working directory no longer picks one.

- `cli.rs`: `ReadOnlyGlobals` loses `config` [2] and `namespace` [3]. The
  root help's `GLOBAL_OPTIONS` list shrinks with them. `check` moves from
  `Globals` to `ReadOnlyGlobals`, losing `--dry-run` and `--yes` [1]. `--marketplace`
  stays on `build`, `check` and `bump`. Unknown commands keep going through
  `report_parse_error`, which maps clap's errors to `EXIT_USAGE`.
- `config.rs` [2]: `workspace_above` and `workspace_members` go.
